mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% annualized over the past two months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase > 0.5pp does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 decline does not correlate with subsequent recessionary environment.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 1% does not correlate with subsequent strengthening supply-side fundamentals.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease does not correlate with subsequent easing monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS does not correlate with subsequent strengthening consumer demand.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a tightening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of UNRATE decrease and PAYEMS increase does not correlate with subsequent tightening labor market.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% signals heightened financial conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS increase > 0.25% during tightening cycle does not correlate with subsequent heightened financial conditions.
